mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weekly means (-10.0 to -5.9) and this momentum is self-propagating: each extra week of higher retail footfall pulls more outlets to reopen and more households to resume discretionary shopping, so the next 28-day mean exceeds the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means rose monotonically from -10.0 (t-3w) to -5.9 (t-0w)
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to its trailing 28-day mean of -7.975 despite three consecutive rising weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility is the leading proxy for discretionary trip chains; with TRANSIT improving from -10.4 to -4.3 over two weeks, retail-and-recreation trips chained onto transit journeys rise within two weeks, pulling RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean holds above -6.0 percent for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean falls below its trailing 28-day mean in periods where TRANSIT holds above -6.0 for two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: Return-to-office and transit use must improve jointly for weekday retail footfall to recover; the simultaneous rebound of TRANSIT (-10.4 to -4.3) and WORKPLACES (-13.6 to -2.3) signals restored commuting circuits that feed mall and F&B traffic within two weeks, whereas either series alone does not.
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve versus their prior weekly means, the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, commuting normalisation is the binding constraint on retail-and-recreation; WORKPLACES recovering from a -13.6 trough to -2.1 shows office occupancy returning, and each large gain in WORKPLACES maps into higher weekday retail footfall within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean recovers by more than 8 points from its trailing four-week low
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES low of -13.6 at t-2w followed by -2.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: The forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above the trailing 28-day mean in the four weeks after WORKPLACES recovers more than 8 points from its four-week low.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM at +39.4 is a precautionary at-home provisioning signal: households are still spending on staples rather than discretionary retail, so as this series decays toward baseline the spending mix rotates back into RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM eased from 40.7 (t-1w) to 39.4 (t-0w) while RETAIL_REC rose
failure_condition: In weeks where GROCERY_PHARM drops below 39.0, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has improved 7.9 points over three weeks (-23.6 to -15.7), a mid-year outdoor-activity season signal; outdoor leisure trips spill over into adjacent retail and F&B catchments, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean improves by at least 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: After two consecutive week-on-week PARKS gains of at least 2 points, the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not above the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The retail recovery is transit-dependent: if TRANSIT reverses back below -6.0 the discretionary trip chain breaks and RETAIL_REC falls within one week, because the current upturn has no independent footfall source once transit demand stalls.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped to -10.4 at t-2w before recovering to -4.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT falls below -6.0, the following 7-day RETAIL_REC mean is not lower than its preceding 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The reopening bounce is one-off: while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5.0 and GROCERY_PHARM above 39, households retain stay-home provisioning, so the retail rebound stalls and mean-reverts lower over two weeks even as headline mobility looks stable.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays above 5.0 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 39.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 5.3 and GROCERY_PHARM at 39.4 at t-0w, both above baseline
regime_hint: partial reopening with residual stay-home behaviour
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL holds above 5.0 and GROCERY_PHARM above 39.0 for two consecutive weeks, the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is higher than the trailing 28-day mean.
